story.title: JOUP COFFEE
story.subtitle: An ecosystem
story.text1: A space where education, technique and business development come together to transform the way Argentina experiences coffee.
story.text2Continue: , including baristas, instructors, roasters, coffee shop owners and enthusiasts who today work behind the bar, in gastronomic projects, in roasteries or teaching in different parts of the world.
story.text3: We are a constantly growing community, united by a single idea: elevating coffee culture through training, quality and collaboration.
story.text4: JOUP COFFEE was born as a community-School, grew as a laboratory and today functions as a comprehensive platform that drives people, businesses and projects.
story.arrowText: Our identity is sustained by three pillars that shape everything we do:

philosophy.title: A CLEAR PHILOSOPHY
philosophy.text1: JOUP exists because we believe that coffee is culture, identity, craft and opportunity.
philosophy.text2: Because we are committed to local growth, traceability, transparency and the development of a fairer and more professional ecosystem.
philosophy.text3: We believe in training as an engine, in community as a network, in technique as a foundation and in collaboration as a path.
philosophy.text4: That's why we work together with coffee shops, companies, institutions, professionals and collaborators who share a vision:
philosophy.text5: making coffee a space of encounter, excellence and shared purpose.

lab.title: JOUP LAB
lab.description: The academy where we train the new generation of coffee professionals, where we study, analyze and live coffee.
lab.details: We create intermediate and advanced courses, ONE & ONE programs, internal training and an educational proposal that combines technical clarity, deep sensory skills and unique pedagogy. We teach to transform. So that more people have access to real, modern and demanding training. So that knowledge elevates the craft.

studio.title: JOUP STUDIO
studio.description: Comprehensive solutions for specialty coffee projects.
studio.details: We accompany openings, optimize operations, design spaces, standardize processes and build brands with identity, aesthetics and digital presence. We help entrepreneurs, teams and established businesses grow with criteria, order and professionalism. From technical consulting to web design, branding, food photography, filmmaking and project management: JOUP STUDIO integrates all the necessary areas for a coffee business to function with quality and coherence.

courses.sectionSubtitle: Programs designed to train specialty coffee professionals

fundamentals.title: COFFEE FUNDAMENTALS
fundamentals.description: The conceptual and technical foundation for understanding coffee as a system. This axis builds criteria on extraction, methods, sensory skills, and bar work, moving from mechanical repetition to understanding what you do and why. It's the starting point that supports the entire journey within Joup Coffee Lab.

intermediate.name: Intermediate
intermediate.subtitle: Solid foundation with real criteria
intermediate.intro: This level is for those who already work with coffee (or have completed a basic course) and want to stop 'doing by repetition' and start understanding what's happening in the cup. We build fundamentals that later support everything: espresso, filtered coffee, milk, sensory skills, and service.
points: Extraction framework: ratio, grind, time, temperature, turbulence, and how they relate.
Useful barista language: varietals, processes, roasting, freshness, grinding, water—what's necessary to avoid speaking in generalities.
Correction criteria: detecting whether the problem is recipe, technique, grinder, water, roast, or coffee.
Professional routine: work order, cleanliness, consistency, and daily control.
intermediate.result: Joup Result: you leave with a foundation that shows at the bar: less chance, more control, and a clear way to explain what you do.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.subtitle: Professional consistency, fine reading, and standards
advanced.intro: We train real consistency, applied sensory reading, and fine correction. It's not 'more information': it's more precision. Your goal stops being 'make it tasty' and becomes 'make it the same, good, every day, with criteria'
points: Technical-sensory diagnosis: translating flavor into variables (acidity vs under-extraction, bitterness vs compound over-degradation, astringency vs channeling, etc.).
Applied protocols: quality control, simple triangulations, recording, documented adjustments.
Deep corrections: how to maintain the cup when the batch, climate, flow, grinder, or demand changes.
Service standard: consistency, customer communication, and the bar as a system.
advanced.result: Joup Result: you go from executor barista to barista with your own technical criteria.

espresso.title: ESPRESSO & CALIBRATION
espresso.description: Espresso control turned into method. We work the relationship between grind, dose, yield, flow, and sensory reading to achieve real consistency in the coffee shop. Here espresso stops being intuition and becomes technical control and professional criteria.

intermediate.name: Intermediate
intermediate.subtitle: Solid calibration, no magic
intermediate.intro: This course teaches you to calibrate espresso repeatably. The focus is on building a routine that works in a real coffee shop: times, doses, yield, flow, and simple adjustments with logic.
points: Methodical dial-in: what to move first and why (grind / ratio / time).
Shot reading: crema, flow, color, time, sensory.
Critical variables: distribution, leveling, puck prep, dose consistency.
Daily stability: how to adapt the recipe when humidity, temperature, or coffee aging changes.
intermediate.result: Joup Result: you calibrate faster, with less trial and error, and defend your recipe with foundations.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.subtitle: Total control: extraction, flow, and consistency under pressure
advanced.intro: Here we enter applied extractology. We work as serious teams work: we measure, interpret, adjust, and leave a stable system. This is for those who want to be above average.
points: Extraction curves and flow reading: how they impact sweetness, clarity, and texture.
TDS / yield / balance (if there's a refractometer, we use it; if not, we train the equivalent sensory reading).
Advanced channeling: real causes and how to correct them (puck prep, grind, distribution, pressure, basket).
Volume calibration: maintaining quality when there's a line, stress, and changing hands.
Recipe optimization per coffee: not all coffees 'ask for the same thing.'
advanced.result: Joup Result: you master espresso as a system: repeatable, defensible, and scalable.

sensory.title: SENSORY & CUPPING
sensory.description: Joup's training core. This axis develops sensitivity, language, and sensory criteria to evaluate coffees with clarity, detect defects, and make professional decisions. Training the palate is training the foundation of everything else.

intermediate.name: Intermediate
intermediate.subtitle: Trained sensitivity + lexicon
intermediate.intro: This level is the gateway to what differentiates a common barista from one with a future: knowing how to taste. We train sensitivity to detect basic defects, describe with clarity, and build a real vocabulary.
points: Main attributes: fragrance/aroma, flavor, acidity, sweetness, body, aftertaste, balance.
Basic defects and probable causes: dirty ferment, phenols, astringency, mold, etc.
Triangulations: learning to distinguish subtle changes with method.
Functional lexicon: describing without exaggeration, with precision and coherence.
intermediate.result: Joup Result: you start trusting your palate and communicating it professionally.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.subtitle: Protocol, critical criteria, and deep reading
advanced.intro: Here the training changes: it's no longer 'discovering flavors', it's building professional sensory criteria. You learn to evaluate with standards, to argue, and to make decisions: coffee selection, profile, roasting, use.
points: Serious cupping protocol: consistency, recording, comparison, panel calibration.
Structure analysis: acidity (type and quality), sweetness (form and persistence), texture, finish, cleanliness.
Complex defect detection: problematic fermentations, phenolics, greens, aging, damage.
Applied interpretation: what coffee works for what (espresso, filter, milk) and why.
advanced.result: Joup Result: your palate stops being 'opinion' and becomes a professional tool.

filtered.title: FILTERED COFFEE
filtered.description: Coffee expressed with clarity and precision. Filtering methods are approached as tools for extraction control and sensory exploration, integrating technique, attention, and coffee reading. A space where method and experience meet.

intermediate.name: Intermediate
intermediate.subtitle: Essential technique: clarity, consistency, and recipes that work
intermediate.intro: For baristas who want to stop depending on 'internet recipes' and learn to build their own with foundations. V60, press, AeroPress (and logic transferable to any method).
points: Smart base recipe: ratio, grind, temperature, target times.
Pouring and turbulence: how they affect extraction and clarity.
Bloom and saturation control: when it helps and when it hinders.
Typical errors: astringency, dryness, emptiness, bitterness, sharp acidity.
intermediate.result: Joup Result: clean, consistent filtered coffee, and a method to adjust without improvisation.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.subtitle: Total extraction control: bypass, leaching, and profile design
advanced.intro: This level is for those who want to truly master filtered coffee. You learn to design profiles: more clarity, more texture, more sweetness, or more acidity—by choice—and sustain it.
points: Bypass and concentration: when to use it, how it affects structure and perception.
Leaching and staged extraction: how the bed 'empties' and what it means in the cup.
Advanced grinding: particle distribution, fines, filter channels.
Complex recipes: multiple pours, temperature control, intentional agitation.
Service consistency: replicability at the bar.
advanced.result: Joup Result: signature filtered coffee with foundation, not by chance.

latteArt.title: LATTE ART
latteArt.description: Technique, control, and aesthetics in balance. Latte Art works milk steaming and pouring as a natural extension of espresso and service. The figure is a consequence of technical mastery, not the final goal.

intermediate.name: Intermediate
intermediate.subtitle: Real microfoam + pitcher control (perfect base figures)
intermediate.intro: This level organizes the technique so latte art isn't 'sometimes yes, sometimes no'. Here we build fine muscle: texturize, integrate, and pour with control.
points: Professional texturing: proper aeration, integration, shine, density.
Pitcher control: height, speed, angle, entry point.
Base figures: heart, tulip, simple rosetta with cleanliness and symmetry.
Error correction: bubbles, dry foam, 'heavy' milk, flow cut.
intermediate.result: Joup Result: your figures become repeatable and your cup looks like it's from a 'serious coffee shop.'

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.subtitle: Complex free pour + millimetric control
advanced.intro: Here technique becomes aesthetic. We work precision, timing, symmetry, and composition. It's not 'making little drawings': it's mastering fluid + texture + movement.
points: Texture by style: cappuccino, flat white, latte—and how pouring changes.
Complex figures: advanced rosettas, multiple tulips, swans/compositions (depending on group level).
Consistency under pressure: replicating in real service.
Fine diagnosis: micro-failures of milk, pitcher, temperature, steaming, and pouring.
advanced.result: Joup Result: your latte art starts speaking for you without you having to explain it.

processing.title: PROCESSING & GREEN COFFEE
processing.description: The origin of flavor. This axis connects varietals, processes, and farm decisions with their impact in the cup, building criteria to interpret, evaluate, and select origin coffees with foundation.

intermediate.name: Intermediate
intermediate.subtitle: Classic processes and their real impact on flavor
intermediate.intro: This level teaches you to read coffee from origin: not 'what is a natural', but what changes sensorially, what to expect, and how to identify it in the cup.
points: Washed / honey / natural: impact on sweetness, acidity, cleanliness, texture.
Main varietals: what they tend to contribute and how to recognize them.
Freshness and storage: aging, aromatic loss, typical defects.
Applied sensory reading: relating process to profile without falling into clichés.
intermediate.result: Joup Result: your coffee discourse becomes serious and your coffee selection improves.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.subtitle: Modern fermentations + critical green coffee evaluation
advanced.intro: Here we enter the complex: modern processes, directed fermentations, and the most important part: criteria to distinguish innovation from defect.
points: Complex fermentations: what they seek, what risks they bring, how they're perceived.
Defects vs 'funk': detecting phenolics, mold, over-fermentation, contamination.
Critical evaluation: lot consistency, cleanliness, structure, and purpose of use.
Bar selection: what process works for espresso, filter, milk, and why.
advanced.result: Joup Result: you go from trend consumer to professional who evaluates and decides.

science.title: COFFEE SCIENCE
science.description: The logic behind extraction. Physics and chemistry principles are applied to understand pressure, temperature, solubility, and flow, and thus diagnose and optimize results. Thinking of coffee as a system.

intermediate.name: Intermediate
intermediate.subtitle: Physics and chemistry applied to extraction (to truly understand)
intermediate.intro: This course brings coffee science down to earth without getting academic: what you need to understand why what happens happens.
points: Solubility and extraction: what extracts first, what later, and how it feels.
Temperature, time, grind: real relationship (not clichés).
Pressure and resistance: espresso vs filter, what changes and why.
Typical errors explained with logic: astringency, bitterness, aggressive acidity, lack of sweetness.
intermediate.result: Joup Result: you stop calibrating by intuition and start calibrating with understanding.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.subtitle: Fluid mechanics + deep extractology
advanced.intro: For those who want to take their level to 'top' territory. We work fluid dynamics applied to coffee: flow, permeability, turbulence, channels, and stability.
points: Puck/bed flow and permeability: how it behaves and how to control it.
Intentional turbulence: when it improves and when it ruins.
Extraction models: reading cup structure as 'system result.'
Advanced optimization: consistency, repetition, scalability.
advanced.result: Joup Result: you understand coffee as a physical phenomenon and control it as a professional.

pedagogy.title: COFFEE PEDAGOGY
pedagogy.description: Coffee taken to teaching. Oriented to those seeking to train, lead, or transmit knowledge, working on technical communication, class structure, and pedagogical criteria applied to coffee.

integralProgram.name: Integral Program
integralProgram.subtitle: Training for instructors and leaders
integralProgram.intro: Complete program for those seeking to teach, train teams, or lead educational coffee projects. It's not just 'knowing how to do': it's knowing how to transmit, structure, communicate, and sustain pedagogical criteria.
points: Class structure: content design, didactic progression, clear objectives.
Group management: dynamics, attention, constructive correction.
Technical communication: clarity, precision, and adaptation to student level.
Applied public speaking: presence, confidence, and discourse management.
Learning psychology: how we learn, how we retain, how we apply.
integralProgram.result: Joup Result: you go from 'knowing coffee' to 'training coffee professionals.'

services.heroSubtitle: Comprehensive solutions for specialty coffee projects
services.visionText: Transform specialty coffee projects into sustainable, professional businesses with their own identity through a comprehensive approach that combines technique, strategy and operational criteria.
services.descriptionMain: JOUP STUDIO is the consulting and project development area of JOUP. We work with entrepreneurs, established coffee shops and businesses seeking to professionalize their operation, optimize their processes and build a solid identity in the specialty coffee market.

consulting.title: Comprehensive Consulting
consulting.description: Complete accompaniment from idea to operation: viability analysis, business model, equipment selection and proposal design.

architecture.title: Bar Architecture
architecture.description: Functional space design optimized for operational efficiency, workflow and customer experience.

optimization.title: Operational Optimization
optimization.description: Process standardization, waste reduction, cost control and profitability improvement with technical criteria.

training.title: Professional Training
training.description: Technical and sensory training for teams: espresso, filtered coffee, latte art, calibration and quality service.

branding.title: Branding & Identity
branding.description: Brand development, visual identity, web design (by TukiCode), food photography and digital strategy.

protocols.title: Quality Protocols
protocols.description: Creation of operational standards, replicable recipes, evaluation criteria and control systems.

services.approachText: We work with a personalized approach that adapts to each project. We don't offer generic solutions: we analyze, design and implement specific strategies based on operational reality, business objectives and market context.
services.approachHighlight: We combine technical knowledge, strategic vision and real experience in the specialty coffee industry so your project works with professionalism, consistency and clarity.

serviceProcess.title: HOW WE WORK
serviceProcess.description: At JOUP STUDIO we design comprehensive processes to accompany, optimize and professionalize specialty coffee shops. Each service responds to a real business need: from the architectural design of the bar to team training, recipe standardization, cost optimization and building experiences that build loyalty. Our approach combines technique, criteria and real operability.

accompaniment.intro: A clear, professional, and customized process. We accompany specialty coffee projects from the initial idea to real operation, with a comprehensive approach that combines technique, concept, aesthetics, and functionality. Our work is not limited to opening a coffee shop: we seek for it to function well, have identity, and be sustainable over time.
accompaniment.subtitle: Your Journey with JOUP STUDIO

architecture.intro: Designing a space that works in favor of coffee, the team, and the business. At JOUP we understand coffee architecture as an operational tool, not as an isolated aesthetic exercise. A poorly designed bar generates errors, stress, waste, and low quality, even with good coffee and a good team. This process seeks to design spaces that function under pressure, maintain quality, and accompany the project's growth.
architecture.subtitle: Coffee Architecture & Bar Design Process

training.intro: Training a team that operates with technique, consistency, and identity. Having good coffee, correct machines, and well-designed space is not enough if the team doesn't understand what they're doing, why they're doing it, and how to sustain it daily. This process seeks for your baristas not to just execute recipes, but to understand, apply criteria, and generate quality autonomously. The training adapts to your service model and your team's level, integrating technique, sensory skills, and work philosophy.
training.subtitle: Building a High-Performance Team

curingprocesshopperselection.intro: Your coffee hopper is not a decoration: it's the first filter of your quality. Choosing coffees with criteria, not by trend or price, directly impacts the sensory profile, operational consistency, and business projection. This process combines coffee curation, profile analysis, and hopper design according to your bar's concept and real operation. The goal is for your menu to make sense, your coffees to be coherent with each other, and for you to have clear selection criteria.
curingprocesshopperselection.subtitle: Strategic Hopper Design

coffeeWasteCostOptimization.intro: Coffee waste is one of the most underestimated problems in the specialty coffee industry. It directly impacts the business's profitability, team efficiency, and operational sustainability. This process seeks to identify, measure, and systematically reduce coffee waste through technical adjustments, recipe optimization, and team training. The goal is not to 'spend less,' but to operate better: with precision, awareness, and clear criteria.
coffeeWasteCostOptimization.subtitle: Operating with Efficiency and Criteria

espressoBrewStandardProcess.intro: Operational consistency is one of the most difficult things to sustain in the specialty coffee bar. Having good coffee, machines, and trained baristas is not enough if each preparation is different, if results are inconsistent, or if quality drops at times of high volume. This process seeks to build technical protocols for espresso and filtered coffee, designed to be replicated daily, under pressure, and with quality. The goal is for your bar to deliver the same result, every time, in any circumstance.
espressoBrewStandardProcess.subtitle: Standardization for Operational Excellence

menuDesignAndOptimization.intro: Your coffee menu is not just a list of drinks: it's your operational tool, your sales discourse, and your quality filter. A poorly designed menu generates confusion in the customer, saturation in the bar, unnecessary costs, and low profitability. This process seeks to build a coherent, efficient menu aligned with the business concept, designed to operate under pressure, sell with clarity, and be sustainable over time.
menuDesignAndOptimization.subtitle: Menu that Works, Communicates, and Sells

customerExperienceAndService.intro: Coffee quality is not the only thing your customer perceives. Service experience, space, attention, order, and general coherence directly influence how your product is valued. This process seeks to design a comprehensive customer experience aligned with your coffee shop's concept and type of service. We work on the customer journey, service flows, staff communication, and operational details that build loyalty and differentiate.
customerExperienceAndService.subtitle: Designing Experiences that Differentiate and Build Loyalty

monitoringAndContinuousImprovement.intro: Excellence is not achieved in a day: it is built with time, criteria, and continuous adjustments. This final phase of the process seeks to accompany the operation beyond opening, with systematic monitoring, data analysis, and operational optimizations. The goal is for your bar to continue evolving, adjusting, and improving with foundation, consistency, and clarity.
monitoringAndContinuousImprovement.subtitle: Sustained Growth with Criteria

step1.title: First Contact
step1.description: Understanding your vision before proposing solutions
step1.details: The first step is to listen. We meet to understand your idea, your context, your goals, and the real moment of the project. We don't offer closed packages: we design accompaniment based on what you need today and where you want to go. This meeting defines the tone of the entire process.

step2.title: Project Analysis
step2.description: Reading the business before designing it
step2.details: We analyze the project's viability from a strategic and operational perspective: location, target audience, value proposition, competition, available resources, and real scope. Based on this diagnosis, we define priorities, timelines, and work focuses. Without analysis, there are no good decisions.

step3.title: Concept Design
step3.details: We develop the comprehensive concept of your coffee shop: service philosophy, gastronomic proposal, coffee menu, customer experience, and brand guidelines. The goal is for everything to make sense, be coherent, and have its own personality. This is where the project's identity is born.

step4.title: Equipment Selection
step4.description: Technology aligned with your concept and budget
step4.details: We advise on choosing espresso machines, grinders, brewing methods, and general equipment according to work volume, service style, and business projection. We seek efficiency, durability, and technical coherence, not unnecessary over-equipment.

step5.title: Coffee Curation
step5.description: Choosing coffees with criteria, not by trend
step5.details: We select the coffees that best adapt to your proposal and design specific usage profiles and preparation methods. The curation considers origin, process, sensory profile, consistency, and bar viability. Coffee accompanies the concept, it doesn't contradict it.

step6.title: Team Training
step6.description: Training people, not just teaching recipes
step6.details: We train the team in technique, sensory skills, service, and work philosophy. We seek for them to understand what they do, why they do it, and how to maintain quality on a daily basis. A good project needs an aligned team.

step7.title: Setup and Calibration
step7.details: We install and calibrate equipment, adjust recipes, optimize workflows, and define quality protocols. Everything is prepared to operate with order, consistency, and clarity from day one.

step8.title: Opening and Follow-up
step8.details: We are present at the opening and offer subsequent follow-up to adjust processes, resolve doubts, and accompany the project's growth. Excellence is not achieved in a day: it is built with time and criteria.

step1.title: First contact and project understanding
step1.details: We begin with a deep conversation to understand the entrepreneurship's vision, service type, target audience, and expected volume. We don't design the same for a grab-and-go coffee shop as for an experience space or gastronomic café. We define: operational objectives, service expectations, and real space limitations.

step2.title: Technical space analysis
step2.description: Studying the venue from a functional logic
step2.details: We study the venue from a functional logic: team circulation, client-bar relationship, congestion points, preparation zones, dispatch and cleaning areas, barista ergonomics. We detect bottlenecks before they exist.

step3.title: Bar design oriented to real service
step3.description: The bar as an efficient work system
step3.details: We design the bar as a work system: strategic location of machines and grinders, espresso, milk and filter flows, real support surfaces, access to cleaning and disposal, reduction of unnecessary movements. Every decision responds to efficiency, consistency, and control.

step4.title: Aesthetic integration with project identity
step4.details: Visual design accompanies function. Materials, colors, and layout reinforce the concept without compromising operability or maintenance.

step5.title: Operational validation and final adjustments
step5.details: Before closing the design, we validate operation in real service scenarios and make adjustments to ensure the space is sustainable over time.

step1.title: Diagnosis and level detection
step1.description: Understanding the team before training them
step1.details: Before teaching anything, we detect: current level of technique, sensory skills, work habits, and potential areas for improvement. Not all teams need the same. We adapt the training to your service reality and operational priorities.

step2.title: Technical and sensory training
step2.description: Building real foundations: technique, palate, and criteria
step2.details: We train the team in espresso and filtered coffee technique, foam control, latte art, sensory calibration, and extraction reading. The goal is for each barista to understand what they're doing, not just memorize steps. We work on: machine operation, espresso extraction, milk treatment, filtering methods, palate training, and adjustments by taste.

step3.title: Quality and service protocols
step3.details: We establish work protocols: extraction times, grinder adjustment, temperature control, cleanliness, dispatch order, service flow, and error handling. These protocols are designed so the team operates with autonomy, consistency, and clarity.

step4.title: Real operation accompaniment
step4.description: Training under pressure and in real service
step4.details: We accompany the team in real operation: training during service, in-the-moment calibration, technique correction, and quality control. This is where knowledge is truly consolidated, not in an empty bar.

step5.title: Autonomy and continuous improvement
step5.description: Building an autonomous and evolving team
step5.details: The final step is that the team learns to calibrate, adjust, and improve without constant external supervision. We train leaders within the team and establish continuous monitoring and training dynamics. A good team continues to grow over time.

step1.title: Concept definition and target profile
step1.description: What coffee do you want to offer? Why?
step1.details: We start by defining the sensory direction you want for your bar: more acidity or more sweetness, floral or chocolate, clean or complex, exotic or accessible, espresso-oriented or filter. This defines the selection criteria.

step2.title: Coffee selection and sensory analysis
step2.description: Tasting, analyzing, and deciding with criteria
step2.details: We taste lots from different roasters and origins, analyzing them from a sensory and operational perspective: cleanliness, consistency, extraction versatility, performance in milk, service viability, and alignment with the concept. We don't select by price or trend: we select by criteria.

step3.title: Strategic hopper design
step3.description: Building a coherent and functional menu
step3.details: We design the coffee hopper according to operational logic: number of selections, sensory diversity, espresso and filter role, seasonal rotation, and supply consistency. The hopper must make sense with the bar's concept, size, and type of customer.

step4.title: Profile adjustment and recipe calibration
step4.details: Each coffee has its optimal extraction profile. We calibrate espresso and filter recipes for each selection, adjusting grind, dose, temperature, and time according to sensory performance. This is what makes the difference between 'having good coffee' and 'extracting good coffee.'

step5.title: Rotation and supply consistency
step5.details: We establish a rotation system that allows keeping the menu updated without compromising operational consistency. We define reorder frequency, seasonal changes, and contingency criteria. The idea is that selection is dynamic, but not chaotic.

step1.title: Waste diagnosis and quantification
step1.details: We analyze and quantify coffee waste in different operational areas: calibration, recalibration, errors, excessive doses, grinder purge, staff drinks, handling, and packaging. We identify critical points and determine the real impact on business cost.

step2.title: Critical point detection
step2.description: Where waste is generated and why
step2.details: We detect why waste is generated: lack of calibration, over-dosing, inconsistent grind, frequent recipe changes, lack of team criteria, deficient equipment. We analyze the root cause, not just the symptom.

step3.title: Technical and operational optimization
step3.description: Adjusting systems to reduce unnecessary waste
step3.details: We optimize espresso recipes, grinder calibration, purge protocols, and dose control. We work on precision, not saving: the goal is to waste less because we operate better, not because we 'skimp.'

step4.title: Team training in efficiency and awareness
step4.description: A conscious team is an efficient team
step4.details: We train the team in responsible coffee handling, real impact of waste, measurement techniques, and conscious operation. We don't seek stinginess: we seek criteria and respect for the product.

step5.title: Monitoring and continuous adjustment
step5.description: Waste is not eliminated in a day: it's sustained over time
step5.details: We establish monitoring and measurement systems to maintain control over time. The goal is for waste reduction to be sustained, not just an initial effect.

step1.title: Recipe design and extraction calibration
step1.details: We design technical espresso and filter recipes for each coffee, based on TDS measurement, extraction yields, sensory calibration, and replicability. Each recipe has a clear logic and defined adjustment criteria.

step2.title: Quality protocol definition
step2.description: Establishing clear standards for each stage
step2.details: We define extraction, grind, temperature, dose, time protocols, and acceptance and rejection criteria. The idea is that any barista knows what they should achieve and how to verify it.

step3.title: Team sensory calibration
step3.description: Teaching to taste, detect, and adjust
step3.details: We train the team in sensory reading of espresso and filter: how to detect over-extraction, under-extraction, astringency, acidity, bitterness, body imbalance. The idea is for each barista to be their own quality filter.

step4.title: Real operation validation
step4.details: We test recipes and protocols during real service, validating that they work at peak volume, with team rotation, and under pressure. We adjust what doesn't work and validate what does.

step5.title: Recipe documentation and training
step5.description: Recording and transmitting so standards are sustained
step5.details: We document recipes, protocols, and adjustment criteria in a technical and accessible format. We train the team so standards can be sustained over time and with new incorporations.

step1.title: Current menu analysis
step1.description: Understanding what works and what doesn't
step1.details: We analyze the current menu from an operational and commercial perspective: best-selling products, slow products, profitability, complexity, errors, congestion points, and customer perception. We detect opportunities and problems.

step2.title: Concept redefinition and coherence
step2.description: Building an identity that makes sense
step2.details: We work on the menu's conceptual coherence: what you want to communicate, who your customer is, what differentiates you, and how to transmit it through product offer. The menu must have personality and be coherent with the business concept.

step3.title: Product optimization and simplification
step3.description: Simplifying without losing quality or identity
step3.details: We reduce complexity, eliminate products that don't work, simplify recipes, optimize ingredients, and design versions that are more efficient to execute. We seek for the menu to be strong, clear, and operational.

step4.title: Pricing and strategic profitability
step4.description: Selling with criteria, not by intuition
step4.details: We design pricing strategy based on real costs, perception, competition, and strategic positioning. We define margins, combos, sizes, and commercial tactics that make the menu sustainable.

step5.title: Visual and operational implementation
step5.details: We design the visual menu, communication system, staff discourse, and service protocols. The menu must be easy to understand, attractive, and executable by the team.

step1.title: Customer journey mapping
step1.details: We analyze the comprehensive customer journey: from arriving at the coffee shop until leaving. We identify touchpoints, frictions, waiting moments, opportunities for differentiation, and key interactions. We understand how the customer perceives each stage.

step2.title: Service flow optimization
step2.details: We optimize order, preparation, payment, and delivery flows. The goal is for the customer not to feel abandoned, for wait to be perceived as acceptable, and for service to flow without saturation or chaos.

step3.title: Customer communication and education
step3.description: Teaching your customer to value what you do
step3.details: We design communication and education strategies so the customer understands and values what they're consuming. We train the team to communicate techniques, origins, profiles, and concept without being pedantic or aggressive.

step4.title: Ambiance and operational details
step4.description: The small things that build large experiences
step4.details: We work on details that build experience: cleanliness, order, music, temperature, aromas, visual presentation, cup quality, and general coherence. Everything adds up or subtracts.

step5.title: Loyalty and continuous experience
step5.details: We design loyalty strategies based on experience consistency, service quality, and real value generation. The idea is not to 'sell more,' but to build an audience that returns because they feel identified.

step1.title: Periodic data analysis and KPI monitoring
step1.details: We establish measurement and analysis systems for key indicators: extraction yields, coffee consumption, waste, times, sales, profitability, and customer satisfaction. We turn data into decisions.

step2.title: Continuous adjustments and optimizations
step2.description: Evolution based on criteria, not improvisation
step2.details: We review and adjust: extraction protocols, recipes, operation flows, menu, pricing, and strategies. We continuously optimize and systematically improve. The goal is for your bar to continue evolving, growing, and improving over time.
